A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TTPL/MVDF research. Their main text, equations, code listings, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including the relocated checklist and renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original TTPL/MVDF experiments on synthetic TSP/CVRP, TSPLIB, and CVRPLIB, alongside projection, augmentation, and distribution-shift analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds backbone comparisons, LLM sensitivity results, and projection-search timings in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The evolutionary projection search, KNN-based inference, MVDF aggregation, and RRC procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and all six Appendix C projection code listings retain their operations; edited prompt wording and tests with other models do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic TSP/CVRP coverage, TSPLIB/CVRPLIB instances, and clustered, explosion, and implosion distributions. Appendix E reuses TSP1K/5K/10K for additional model configurations rather than introducing datasets or distinct task scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 12 expands the backbone comparison beyond Table 6's POMO KNN/seed controls to paired greedy-versus-TTPL comparisons for POMO, SIGD, BQ, and LEHD. The main benchmark comparator roster is unchanged. Table 4 no longer displays its projection-control comparators, although related comparisons remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds controlled comparisons with and without TTPL across four backbones and tests Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, and Qwen alongside GPT-4o-mini. Existing stated sample sizes, capacities, evaluation metrics, KNN size, and RRC iteration budget are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E substantially expands supplementary evaluation through backbone adaptability tests, LLM-choice sensitivity, and projection-search overhead measurements. These test distinct applicability and cost questions beyond the earlier POMO and distribution-shift studies. Conversely, Table 4 replaces the dedicated projection ablation with a duplicate of the MVDF comparison, weakening that analysis's presentation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental random seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both checklists answer No to statistical significance reporting. The new LLM comparison supplies point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 12–14 add backbone, LLM, and search-time results. CVRPLIB RRC entries are revised: Li_30 changes from 2.02% to 4.46%, Li_31 from 3.82% to 2.73%, and the overall gap from 7.34% to 7.50% in Tables 3 and 10. Main synthetic results remain unchanged. Table 4's former projection results are replaced by duplicated MVDF results, not evidence of a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 and Appendix C's projection formulations retain their mathematical substance. Regrouped equations, renamed clipped-coordinate notation, and rewritten explanatory prose do not introduce new definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: inference-time projection learning without backbone retraining, MVDF, and generalization from 100-node training instances to TSP/CVRP instances up to 100K nodes. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E.3 newly interprets the LLM comparison as showing that LLM choice does not significantly influence projection performance, without statistical uncertainty analysis. Existing explanations of distribution alignment and the limitation concerning slow evolutionary optimization remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a TTPL source-code address in the abstract and reports projection-search times of 5.5, 9.6, and 19.9 hours for TSP1K, TSP5K, and TSP10K in Table 13. Existing hardware, hyperparameter descriptions, and projection implementations are retained; these disclosures do not establish changed training budgets.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.2 discusses EoH, FunSearch, ReEvo, HSEvo, and MCTS-AHD as LLM-based heuristic-design approaches. References also expand to additional routing research. This broadens contextual coverage without substantially changing TTPL's positioning relative to existing NCO approaches.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the main text, prompts, and mathematical explanations; adds TSP/CVRP subsection headings; and moves the checklist before the technical appendices. Affiliations and the conference header are updated, and acknowledgments are added. The main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 12–14, renumbers the license table, and adjusts prompt/code-box pagination and equation grouping. Existing figures retain their visual content. Table 4 now duplicates Table 5 while retaining its projection-ablation caption, introducing a display-content mismatch.

improvement.justification: Appendix E provides useful evidence about backbone and LLM dependence and quantifies previously unreported projection-search costs; the code address also improves access information. These yield a limited net gain in evidence and transparency. Gains are tempered by the duplicated Table 4 and Appendix D.1's stale 7.34% statement despite revised 7.50% tables. Much of the displaced projection-gap evidence remains available in Tables 1–2.
